runs.name: Shopify Inc.
runs.entry: Price **$170.85** (close 2026-10-09, aggregator, flagged) x **1,286,643,931 shares** (Class A plus Class B, 10-Q cover as of 2026-07-31, 0001594805-26-000047; the Founder Share excluded) = cap **$219.8B**; sovereign **5.60%** (UST 30Y). Primary document the FY2025 10-K (0001594805-26-000007, filed 2026-02-11), FY2025 operating cash $2,033M cross-checked to the filed statement and FY2021's $504.4M to the 40-F. Q1 TOO HARD (NATURE): the filer calls its market "characterized by constant change and innovation" and "transforming", ties success to its "vision for agentic commerce" without building its own AI models, and runs Shopify Payments on Stripe and PayPal agreements renewing every 12 months; the deciding variables (share of GMV on Shopify in ten years and the take rate, 2.21% in 2023, 2.33% in 2025) are ones the filer itself will not forecast. Q2 to Q12 not reached. Beneath the stop, COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash after stock pay, capital spending, net loan originations and acquisitions, interest income out after tax, $19M / $(2,712)M / $(461)M / $422M / $653M for 2021-2025, mean $(416)M (2022 carries a $1.75B logistics acquisition sold for stock in 2023 with a $1.34B impairment); the series changes sign, so specific (b) gives the no-growth case alone: range $(1.52) a share all-equity ($(3.56) equity-only), fair $1.02 all-equity ($(2.00) equity-only); generous non-convention cases (2025 alone grown 25.8% ten years) $13.32-$71.53, fair $22.23, or $22.13-$136.96, fair $39.71, with loans not deducted; every case below the price. Balance sheets FY2016-FY2025: paid-in capital $0.47B to $10.4B, the 2025 surplus largely unrealized gains on equity investments, the lending book 3% to 15% of revenue ($1.78B; $2.18B mid-2026), no debt at 2026-06-30 after the convertible was settled in 2025, cash and securities $5.47B. Competitors not reached; the 10-K names only categories of rival. Facts after the stop, not weighed: buybacks $1.93B at an average $114.63 in the first half of 2026; the founder holds 40% to 49.9% of the votes; CEO 2025 pay $35M in options. No integrity facts found. Analyst's confessed conventions: net loan originations as capital spending, interest income out at the 18.4% effective rate, equity investments beside net cash, not in it. Analyst's gaps for the operator: (1) no rule for a negative no-growth case or for non-cash sale proceeds in the window; (2) a lending book inside an operating company is not named by the range convention; (3) the all-equity basis does not say whether equity investments at fair value count; (4) the brief's competitor instruction is empty when the 10-K names no rivals; (5) specific (a) covers only an aberrational first or last window year, not middle years. Self-audit confesses the run was drafted in one pass and committed at Q1's close (two commits, 212b488b and 7b1e2ec5), and that the 40-F statements for FY2016-FY2020 and FY2022-FY2023 were transcribed from XBRL, not opened; the 2018 loan figure is marked unchecked; the research folder's q7_output.txt equity-only line wrongly adds net cash (the run file carries the correct $(3.56)). Dispatcher quote check: 14 quoted fragments beside ids, 13 in their rows; the fourteenth is the filer's own phrase in the box line ("characterized by constant change and innovation", from the 10-K) set beside M2000-104, L1993-023 and M2000-105 as the rule cited, not offered as the rows' words; recorded, not fixed. No alert (box not OUT at Q7 or IN); v4.1 bands retired. Position note filled at the fold: not held. check_framework PASS.
runs.narr: Q1 TOO HARD (NATURE): a field the filer itself calls fast-changing and transforming, with payments on Stripe and PayPal rails and AI models it does not build; the ten-year share and take of commerce cannot be foreseen. Beneath the stop the literal range is negative (a cash acquisition sold for stock inside the window), fair $1.02 all-equity against $170.85; even a generous 25.8%-growth case tops out at $136.96. Five framework gaps reported (negative no-growth case, lending book, equity investments in the all-equity basis, empty competitor instruction, middle-year aberrations).
